authGate.description: Every request is checked by your auth service first. A 2xx answer lets it through; anything else (like a redirect to your login page) goes back to the visitor unchanged. Copies of the headers below sent by the visitor are always removed, so they cannot be spoofed.
authGate.urlHelp: http or https, no username or password. Internal addresses are fine.
authGate.copyHeadersLabel: Headers to pass to the app
authGate.copyHeadersHelp: Comma separated, up to 16. Copied from the auth response only when it answers 2xx.
authGate.timeoutHelp: Leave blank to use the server default ({{seconds}}s). If the auth service is down or too slow, visitors get an error, never the app.

errors.urlRequired: Enter the URL of your auth service.
errors.timeout: The timeout must be a whole number of seconds.

authGate.builtinHelp: Visitors sign in with their {{name}} account (including passkeys and two-factor) and only the people below get through. The app receives X-User, X-Email and X-Name.
authGate.builtinUnavailable: Set the platform primary domain first: visitors are sent to the dashboard to sign in.
authGate.allowHelp: Users by email, teams by name, or roles by name.
authGate.allowEmpty: Nobody can get in until you add at least one user, team or role.
authGate.extraHeadersLabel: Extra headers to pass to the app

accessLog.title: Access log
accessLog.empty: No sign-in activity in this time range.
accessLog.loadError: Could not load the access log.

wizard.title: Add a domain, step by step
wizard.description: Point a domain at this app and get a trusted certificate. Each step checks the real state, and nothing is saved until the last one.

domain.label: Domain
domain.invalid: Enter a valid domain, for example app.example.com.
domain.environmentDefault: Default (all environments without their own set)
domain.wwwPreset: Also route {{www}} and redirect it to {{apex}}
domain.apexPreset: Also route {{apex}} and redirect it to {{www}}

dns.propagation: DNS changes usually show up within minutes, but can take up to a few hours depending on the record's TTL. This page re-checks on its own, so you can leave it open.
dns.needDomain: Enter a domain above to see the exact record to add.

port.description: The ingress forwards requests to port {{port}} inside the container.
port.listening: Verified: the container is listening on port {{port}}.
port.otherPort: The container is listening on {{ports}}, not on port {{port}}. Requests would fail until the port matches.
port.notListening: Nothing is listening on port {{port}} inside the running container yet. Check the app starts and binds to 0.0.0.0, not 127.0.0.1.
port.unknown: Not verified: the app is not running yet, or exec access is off for it. The configured port is port {{port}}.
port.execDisabled: Turn on exec access for this app to let the dashboard verify its listening port.
port.notRunning: The app is not running, so its port cannot be verified yet.

certificate.http01: HTTP-01: the certificate is requested automatically once the domain resolves here. Ports 80 and 443 must reach this server from the internet.
certificate.dns01Private: HTTP-01 cannot work: this server's address ({{host}}) is private, so no certificate authority can reach port 80. Use DNS-01 with a wildcard domain such as *.example.com.
certificate.dns01Wildcard: Wildcard domains are validated with DNS-01, which needs a DNS provider connected.
certificate.upstreamProxy: The reverse proxy in front of this server obtains and renews the certificate. Point the domain at this server; the proxy must route it here.
certificate.providerActive: DNS-01 provider: {{provider}}. Certificates for wildcard domains are issued through it.
certificate.providerNone: No DNS-01 provider is connected yet.
certificate.setupStep: Next step: connect Cloudflare, Route53 or Google Cloud DNS on the Domains page, then add a wildcard domain for your zone.
certificate.connectivityNote: This tests the address from the control plane. It cannot prove the port is open to the whole internet, but a closed port here is almost always closed there too.
certificate.stagingNote: Staging certificates are platform-wide, not per app. To test without rate limits, turn on Let's Encrypt staging in the Domains settings first.

googleCloudDns.title: Google Cloud DNS
googleCloudDns.description: Manage records and issue wildcard certificates (DNS-01) through Cloud DNS. Paste a service account JSON key with the DNS Administrator role. If Cloudflare or Route53 is also enabled, they take precedence. Only tested against a local fake of the API.
googleCloudDns.enabledHint: Use Cloud DNS for DNS records and wildcard certificates.
googleCloudDns.keyPlaceholder: Paste the contents of the JSON key file
googleCloudDns.keyPlaceholderSaved: Paste a new key to replace the saved one
googleCloudDns.keySaved: A key is saved. Leave this empty to keep it.
googleCloudDns.keyRequired: A service account JSON key is required to enable Google Cloud DNS.

provider.label: DNS-01 provider
provider.noneHint: Wildcard domains and private-address servers need one.

proxyManaged.line: Certificate managed by your proxy (issued by {{issuer}}, expires {{date}}, renews automatically)
proxyManaged.lineNoIssuer: Certificate managed by your proxy (expires {{date}}, renews automatically)
proxyManaged.unknown: Certificate managed by your proxy. This server has not seen it yet: verify the route on the proxy page.

action.open_port_80: Next step: open ports 80 and 443 to the internet. Check your firewall, your router port forward and your cloud security group, then wait for the next attempt.
action.fix_dns: Next step: point the domain's A or AAAA record at this server, and wait for DNS to propagate.
action.wait_rate_limit: Next step: wait before retrying. The certificate authority is rate limiting this hostname, and every failed attempt counts against the limit.
action.fix_caa: Next step: remove or edit the CAA record so it allows the certificate authority.
action.other_proxy: Another service on this server answers port 80, most likely a reverse proxy such as Traefik or nginx. Either let that proxy issue the certificate and route this domain to Levelrail (see Run behind an existing proxy), or give Levelrail ports 80 and 443.
action.check_logs: Next step: read the ingress logs for the full certificate authority response.

environmentTabs.label: Environment
environmentTabs.defaultHint: Used by any environment that has no domain set of its own.
environmentTabs.activeHint: This app is tagged with this environment, so this set is what the ingress routes.
environmentTabs.inactiveHint: Not routed right now. It starts routing when this app is moved into this environment.
environmentTabs.empty: No domains for this environment. The default set is used there.
environmentTabs.addLabel: Add a domain to this environment
environmentTabs.failed: Could not save the environment domains.
environmentTabs.loadFailed: Could not load the environment domain sets.

clone.copyDomainsHint: A hostname can belong to only one app, so every copied hostname is rewritten.

connectivityCard.title: Reachability
connectivityCard.description: Whether ports 80 and 443 answer on this server's address, and which DNS-01 provider is connected.
connectivityCard.noHost: No public address is known. Set APP_PUBLIC_HOST on the control plane.
connectivityCard.private: This server is on a private address. HTTP-01 cannot work here, use DNS-01 with a wildcard domain.
connectivityCard.closed: Port 80 or 443 does not answer. Open them in your firewall or forward them from your router.
connectivityCard.ok: Ports 80 and 443 answer from this server.

searchVisibility.hiddenHelp: {{domain}} sends a noindex header on every response and serves a disallow-all robots.txt. This is a request well-behaved crawlers honour, not access control: use basic auth to keep people out.
searchVisibility.visibleHelp: Search engines can index this domain. Hide it to keep consoles, staging and internal tools out of results.

reverseProxy.title: Put the dashboard behind your existing proxy
reverseProxy.description: Something else already owns ports 80 and 443 on this server. Enter the domain you want for the dashboard and copy the exact configuration for that proxy.
reverseProxy.none: Nothing else publishes port 80 or 443 on this server, so Levelrail's own ingress can serve the dashboard directly.
reverseProxy.reachable: Reachable: this domain serves the dashboard.

page.title: Domains

page.noMatchBody: Check the spelling or clear the filter.

empty.noAppsBody: A domain routes traffic to an app. Deploy an app first.
empty.title: No domains yet

dns.privateHint: This server is on a private address, so only DNS-01 can issue a certificate.

cert.renewsManual: Uploaded certificate: renew it before it expires

visibility.failed: Could not change search visibility for {{domain}}.

row.wildcardHint: Matches every single label under this domain. Exact domains on other apps still win.

platform.title: Platform settings

addDialog.title: Add domains
addDialog.description: Pick an app and list the domains that should route to it.
addDialog.domainsHint: One per line, or separated by commas.
addDialog.noApps: No apps yet. Deploy an app, then add domains to it.

issue.custom_cert_unresolved: Uploaded certificate not in use, automatic issuance instead. Upload it again.

issue.dns01_unavailable: Wildcard certificate needs a DNS provider. Enable one under DNS settings.
issue.target_unavailable: Not routed: its target is unavailable.

proxyPicker.title: Proxy
proxyPicker.description: Choose which proxy answers on ports 80 and 443. Managed providers get their route files written and reloaded for you. Manual providers show the configuration to add yourself.
proxyPicker.loadFailed: Could not read the proxy status.
proxyPicker.embeddedBody: Levelrail's own ingress serves ports 80 and 443 and handles certificates. Nothing is written to another proxy.
proxyPicker.embeddedDone: Routing now uses the built-in ingress. Route files written to your proxy were removed.
proxyPicker.embeddedFailed: Could not switch to the built-in ingress.
proxyPicker.notDetected: This proxy was not found on this server. Start it with ports 80 and 443 published, then check again.
proxyPicker.manualBody: Levelrail does not change {{proxy}}. Dry run shows the configuration for your domains, you add it by hand, then check again.
proxyPicker.managedBody: Levelrail writes one route file per domain into {{proxy}}, checks it, reloads the proxy and verifies each domain over HTTPS.
proxyPicker.applyDone: Routes applied. Waiting for your proxy to pick them up.
proxyPicker.dryRunFailed: The dry run found a problem.
proxyPicker.manualNoApply: Manual providers are never applied automatically.

changes.title: What would change
changes.none: Nothing to change. Routes are already in place.

inputs.dirHint: The folder your proxy reads route files from. It could not be detected.
inputs.certDir: Certificate directory inside the proxy container
inputs.certDirHint: For example /etc/letsencrypt/live. It could not be detected.

rejected.title: The proxy refused the new routes
rejected.body: Nothing was kept: the files were rolled back and your proxy keeps serving what it had. Fix the problem below, then try again.

proxyPicker.rootOnly: Changing the proxy needs a root account or token.
proxyPicker.applyWaiting: Apply and verify turns on as soon as {{proxy}} is found on this server. Install it above, or check again once it runs.

proxyMissing.title: {{proxy}} is not running on this server yet
proxyMissing.looked: Levelrail looked for a running container that publishes port 80 or 443 and uses a {{proxy}} image. It found none.
proxyMissing.foundOther: Levelrail looked for a {{proxy}} container on ports 80 and 443 and found {{other}} instead.
proxyMissing.installed: Proxy started. Checking what it detected.
proxyMissing.installFailed: The proxy could not be started.

install.title: Install and start {{proxy}} for me
install.body: Levelrail starts an official {{proxy}} container for you, with ports 80 and 443 published. You see the exact plan first.
install.unsupported: Automatic install is available for Traefik only. {{proxy}} needs certificates you provide, so start it yourself or pick another choice.

builtin.title: Go back to the built-in Caddy
builtin.body: Switch back to the ingress that ships with this control plane. Your domains and settings are kept.

elsewhere.title: It runs somewhere else
elsewhere.body: Your proxy runs on another host or under another name. Enter how to reach it, then check again.

plan.title: Exactly what will happen
plan.safety: Only this container is created. Containers you already run are never stopped or removed, and running this twice does not create a second one.

manual.body: These defaults match a standard setup. Change what differs on your server.
manual.saved: Proxy values saved. Check again to look for it.
manual.saveFailed: Could not save the proxy values.

hints.container: The name of the proxy container.

errors.name: Use letters, numbers, dots, dashes or underscores.

errors.host: Enter a host name or address without http://.

proxySetup.title: Make this domain live
proxySetup.description: Your proxy already owns ports 80 and 443. Levelrail writes the routes it needs, then checks that traffic and a certificate arrive.
proxySetup.unavailable: Proxy integration is not available on this server version.
proxySetup.loadFailed: Could not read the proxy status. It will be retried on the next refresh.
proxySetup.waitingDetail: waiting until your proxy is found
proxySetup.setupDone: Routes written. Waiting for your proxy to pick them up.

confirm.title: Write routes to your proxy?

confirm.directoryUnknown: No directory was detected. Fix the missing items first.
confirm.noDomains: No domains yet. Only the dashboard route is written when it has a domain.

certificate.pending: Proxy default certificate, waiting for issuance

facts.title: What Levelrail detected

none.title: No existing proxy detected
none.body: If a proxy runs somewhere Levelrail cannot see it, set it up by hand with the manual guide.

byo.hint: Only needed if you bought a certificate. Otherwise certificates are issued automatically.
byo.applyIssue: The uploaded certificate is stored but not in use: {{issue}}
byo.replaceHint: Replaces the currently uploaded certificate entirely; there is no partial update.
byo.newHint: Used instead of automatic issuance for this domain, starting on the next reconcile pass.
byo.bothRequired: Both a certificate and a private key are required.
byo.revertBody: The uploaded certificate is discarded immediately. If automatic issuance cannot reach this domain, HTTPS will break until a new certificate is uploaded or issued.
byo.revertFailed: Could not revert to automatic TLS.

ingressUpstream.bannerTitle: HTTPS is handled by your proxy
ingressUpstream.bannerBody: This instance does not request certificates. Point your domains at the proxy host, and the proxy terminates TLS and forwards to this ingress.
ingressUpstream.trustedProxiesMissing: No trusted proxy ranges are set (APP_INGRESS_TRUSTED_PROXIES), so forwarded protocol and host headers are ignored.
ingressUpstream.switchLabel: TLS is terminated by a proxy in front
ingressUpstream.switchHelp: Turn this on when Traefik, nginx or Caddy owns ports 80 and 443. This instance then never runs ACME and builds links with the public port.
ingressUpstream.acmeSkipped: Certificate issuance is stored but skipped while a proxy handles HTTPS.
ingressUpstream.portHelp: If a proxy such as Traefik or nginx forwards to this ingress, enter the port clients use (usually 443) so links work.
ingressUpstream.portInvalid: Enter a port between 0 and 65535, or leave it blank.

acmeBlocked.title: Real certificates cannot be issued from here
acmeBlocked.body: Certificate authorities check ports 80 and 443, and this ingress listens on {{http}} and {{https}}. If a proxy such as Traefik or nginx owns those ports, let it handle HTTPS for this domain and turn real certificates off here. Otherwise give Levelrail ports 80 and 443, or use a DNS-01 provider.

dnsCheck.propagatingHelp: Public DNS already points this domain at this server. This server's own resolver keeps a "not found" answer for a while (often up to 30 minutes), so it will connect on its own. Nothing is wrong.
dnsCheck.notFoundHelp: No resolver has this record yet. Check the record at your DNS provider (type, name, value) and give it a minute. A new record is usually visible within a few minutes.

text.propagatingSeen: Waiting for DNS to propagate ({{resolver}} sees it)
text.propagatingWaiting: Waiting for the record to show up in DNS

goLive.proxiedWarning: The record is proxied by Cloudflare. Set the SSL/TLS mode to Full (strict) or visitors can hit redirect loops.
goLive.conflictHint: A different record already exists for this name and was left alone. Remove it, or add the domain again with replace turned on.
goLive.connectCloudflare: No DNS provider is connected, so add the record yourself.
goLive.connectCloudflareAction: Connect Cloudflare to do this automatically.

baseDomain.zoneNotFound: No zone for this name at your DNS provider. Connect a provider that manages it first.

standalone.modeProxy: Proxy to a port or URL
standalone.title: Proxy a domain
standalone.description: Serve a domain from any port on this server, an address on your network, an external URL, another app's port or a container. No app needed.
standalone.listeningNone: No listening ports detected. Type the port your service uses.
standalone.addressHint: An IP or hostname on a private network or the mesh, with its port.
standalone.urlHint: TLS and the Host header follow the URL. A path becomes a prefix.
standalone.appPortHint: Empty uses the app's main port ({{port}}).
standalone.previewEmpty: Pick a target to see where traffic goes.
standalone.upstreamTls: Connect to the target over TLS
standalone.verifyTlsHint: Turn off for a self-signed certificate.
standalone.confirmTitle: This server will connect to an internal target
standalone.confirmCheck: I understand. Route public traffic for this domain to it.
standalone.resultBody: Create the DNS record below, then the certificate is issued automatically.
standalone.unlinkedHint: Not linked to any app. Traffic is proxied to this target.
standalone.removeBody: The route to {{target}} is removed on the next ingress pass. Its settings (auth, WAF, redirects) are removed too.
standalone.pageDescription: Traffic controls for {{domain}}, proxied to {{target}}. Changes apply on the next ingress pass.

serverAddress.title: Server address
serverAddress.description: Point DNS records for your domains at this server.
serverAddress.nat: This address is not on any network interface here, so the server sits behind NAT or a cloud address mapping. Forward ports 80 and 443 to it.
serverAddress.upstream: A proxy in front terminates TLS. Point DNS at that proxy, not at this server.
serverAddress.noneDetected: No public address was detected. Set it below so DNS checks and records are right.
serverAddress.overrideHint: Use this behind a load balancer or when detection is wrong.
serverAddress.recordsNone: Set a public address to see the record to create.

reason.route_unverified: {{proxy}} routes {{domain}}, and this server has not confirmed that {{proxy}} hands its requests to the built-in ingress. The setting is saved, but visitors may not get it. Verify the route to check again.
reason.proxy_unmanaged: {{proxy}} terminates TLS for {{domain}} with a configuration this server does not manage, so it cannot confirm the requests reach the built-in ingress. The setting is saved, but it is not reported as enforced.
reason.not_routed: {{domain}} is not routed yet, so the setting is saved but nothing is enforced.

enforcement.docs: Which controls work behind a proxy

maintenance.activeHint: Visitors to {{domain}} see a fixed maintenance page. The container keeps running; nothing here stops or restarts it.
maintenance.healthOpen: Uptime probes on the readiness path still reach the app

form.title: Page title
form.messagePlaceholder: This site is temporarily unavailable. Please check back soon.
form.plainText: Plain text. Visitors see it as written, without formatting.
form.untilHelp: Optional. Creates a scheduled maintenance entry that also shows on the status page.
form.retryAfterHelp: Sent as Retry-After so clients and crawlers know when to come back. Default 5.
form.bypass: Addresses that still reach the app
form.bypassHelp: IP addresses or CIDR ranges, one per line, up to 32. Use your own address to check the site while it is down.
form.healthBypass: Let uptime probes reach the readiness path
form.maxHoursDefault: Used when no end time is set. Leave empty for the server default of {{hours}} hours, 0 for no limit.
form.maxHoursNone: Safety net when no end time is set. Leave empty for no limit, or enter hours.
form.maxHoursUntil: Not needed: the end time above already ends maintenance.

maintenance.autoOffAt: Switches off on its own at {{date}}
maintenance.noAutoOff: No automatic end, it stays on until you end it

shieldRecommended.title: Abuse protection

shieldRecommended.blockBots: Also refuse known bad bots and AI scrapers
shieldRecommended.preview: {{rate}} requests per minute and {{concurrent}} at once per visitor would be set on {{count}} domain(s).
shieldRecommended.skipped: {{count}} domain(s) already have limits and stay as they are.
